ops.title: Review verdict: render probe bounding (WaitDelay + process group) for v0.38.0
ops.body:
Review of the `internal/render` half of the graphite-gate fix. **Caveat on provenance: this is not an independent adversarial pass.** The codex finder lane (`render-review`) died on "You've hit your weekly limit" before reporting, and subagents were unavailable, so this is the orchestrator reviewing a change it directed — weaker evidence than a second opinion. Worth re-running a finder/refuter pass when capacity returns.

## What changed

Nine `render.RunCLI*` helpers each opened with `exec.CommandContext(...)`; they now share `newCmd`, which additionally sets `WaitDelay = 5s`. A tenth helper, `RunCLIProbeDir`, adds process-group isolation (`Setpgid` + a `Cancel` that SIGKILLs `-pgid`, ESRCH → `os.ErrProcessDone`) via a `render_unix.go`/`render_windows.go` split.

## Findings

**Q1 — `WaitDelay` blast radius across ~115 call sites: acceptable, strictly better than before.** `WaitDelay` bites in two situations. The cancellation path is unaffected in practice, because `CommandContext`'s default `Cancel` already kills the process and `Wait` returns the usual signal `ExitError`. The reachable change is the *normal-exit-with-a-lingering-descendant* path: a child that exits while a descendant still holds the inherited stdout/stderr pipe previously blocked `Wait` **forever**; it now returns `exec.ErrWaitDelay` after 5s with whatever was copied. Every helper treats that as a hard error and discards output, so a command that genuinely succeeded could surface as a failure — but the prior behavior was an unrecoverable hang, so this is an improvement in every case, not a regression. Reachability is low: the plausible candidate, `git gc --auto`/`git maintenance`, daemonizes and redirects its std fds, releasing the pipe.

**Q2 — `RunCLIProbeDir` on the deadline path: correct.** A group SIGKILL surfaces as an `ExitError`, so the `errors.As` branch matches and returns `exitErr.ExitCode()`, which is **-1** for signal termination. That -1 never reaches `classifyGTProbe`: `gtReachable` checks `probeCtx.Err() != nil` first and returns unknown. One benign race — a process exiting at the same instant the deadline fires is classified unknown despite having produced a real answer — which is fail-safe under demote-on-unknown.

**Q3 — the unix `Cancel`: no nil-deref, matches precedent.** `Cancel` is only invoked after a successful start, so `cmd.Process` is non-nil, and `Wait` reaps only after `Cancel` returns, so the unreaped leader does pin the pgid against recycling as the comment claims. Behaviorally identical to `internal/codeexec/discover_unix.go`.

**Q4 — the grandchild test genuinely fails without the fix.** Pointed at the unmodified `RunCLIExitCodeDir` it failed with `grandchild PID 7906 survived cancellation` / `the probe never returned`, then passed in 5.31s against `RunCLIProbeDir`. That is the right falsification — it would not pass if `configureProbeCommand` were a no-op.

**`render_windows.go` sending SIGTERM is correct here, not a defect.** `os.Process.Signal` on Windows supports only `Kill`, so this would misbehave — but it is byte-identical to the existing `internal/codeexec/discover_windows.go`, and goreleaser targets only darwin and linux, so the file exists for compilation hygiene and is never built for release. Consistency with the in-repo precedent beats a correctness fix nobody builds.

## Not defects, checked and dismissed

Per-test timing swings in the render package (89s vs 106s, `TestRunCLIEnv` 31.3s → 10.6s) are pre-existing load noise on this machine, confirmed by re-measuring with `waitDelay = 0`. `WaitDelay` starts its timer only once the child has exited or the ctx is done, so it costs nothing on the normal path.
